clue.text: They're in the kitchen, people cooking with toaster

indicators.note: cooking ingredients transforms them, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene where people are busy making food with a toaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People cooking' reads as cooks at work, but 'cooking' is the signal to rearrange both words together.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelers for spuds are utensils kept in a kitchen drawer, so they are things found in the kitchen.

clue.text: Porridgey offering, long eaten near the Adriatic for starters?

definitions.text: Porridgey offering, long eaten near the Adriatic

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning of a meal, so take the opening letter of each word

parts.words: Porridgey offering, long eaten near the Adriatic
parts.note: the initial letters of the seven words

explanation.surface: A description of a porridge-like dish that has long been a staple along the Adriatic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its initials spell the answer, and read straight it describes the dish, which is eaten in northern Italy on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is a thick maize porridge, a traditional staple of northern Italian cooking.

clue.text: Foxtrot's ending — another dance?

definitions.meaning: the last letter of Foxtrot is T, whose word in the NATO phonetic alphabet is this
second meaning: a ballroom dance, like the foxtrot

explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot and Tango are both NATO alphabet code words as well as dances; the final letter T of 'Foxtrot' is spoken as Tango.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio spelling the letter T is called Tango, and the tango is also an Argentine ballroom dance.

clue.text: Route incorporating avenue is a slog

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body of another, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a trail is a path or route
AV is the abbreviation for avenue

explanation.surface: A road that takes in a long avenue makes for a tiring trek.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the standard abbreviation for avenue, and it goes after the TR of TRAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful, laborious effort, the same idea as a long hard grind or toil.

clue.text: Forbidding words on a sign in WC worried ladylike model within

indicators.note: within means inside, so the following items sit inside the first

parts.note: a privy is a lavatory, like a WC
as in 'what's eating you?', ate means troubled or worried
proper means decorous and respectable
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: A notice on a toilet door bothers a prim model who is inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Three pieces go inside PRIVY, between its V and Y. 'Model' for T is a crossword staple from Ford's Model T car.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a notice keeping trespassers out, so it is a prohibition displayed on a board.

clue.text: Old flame with strong wine and strong beer

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
port is a fortified wine
joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: A former lover turns up with fortified wine and a strong ale.
explanation.walkthrough: Export is a British and especially Scottish name for a stronger-than-usual beer, originally brewed for shipping abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and Britain, an export is a style of stronger, fuller ale, so it names a potent brew.

clue.text: Most important net sales I falsified

indicators.note: falsified figures have been altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An accountant confesses to doctoring the crucial net sales figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsified' reads naturally as cooking the books, which hides its role as the signal to rearrange the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is vital and indispensable, which is the top priority above everything else.

clue.text: Admirers flatter old Russians heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: clothes that suit you flatter you
O is the abbreviation for old
the word with all its middle letters taken out

explanation.surface: Fans fawn over elderly Russians without any real feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a verb about praise, but here it means to look good on, as an outfit does.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitors are men courting a woman, so they are admirers seeking her affection or hand.

clue.text: Family enthralled by magic lantern

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so the word is held inside the following letters

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A family sits spellbound by the pictures of an old magic lantern show.
explanation.walkthrough: A magic lantern was an early slide projector, a parlour entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of related households sharing descent, an extended family.

clue.text: Getting on with ace Baptist, excitable Italian

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: excitable means easily agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An elderly man pals up with a star Baptist and a highly-strung Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excitable' seems to describe the Italian, but it acts on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is getting on means they are ageing, and the idiom for that is being slightly too old.

clue.text: Country record spun, transfixing an American

indicators.note: something spun round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
to transfix is to pierce right through, so one piece runs through the middle of another

parts.note: AN taken as written, plus A for American
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A country music disc is played, captivating a listener from the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record spun' suggests a vinyl disc on a turntable, but the record here is a logbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Angola is a nation on the south-west coast of Africa.

clue.text: Aimlessly nod off in a vehicle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: A taken as written plus a tram, a vehicle

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off on a bus or tram without any particular aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nod off' is a phrase for falling asleep, but the two words split: one is fodder, the other its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at random means with no plan or purpose, which is acting without direction.

clue.text: Musician's cheap shoddy bell shaken

indicators.note: shoddy work is badly made, so these letters are put together wrongly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shaken things are jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer's poor-quality handbell is rattled about.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams, each with its own signal; ''s' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Pachelbel was a German Baroque composer, famous for his Canon in D.

clue.text: That man, in the manner of French, offered up refusal, high and mighty

parts.note: a pronoun for that man
à la is French for 'in the manner of'

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: nay is a refusal

explanation.surface: A man turns down a French-style offer in an arrogant manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High and mighty' reads as haughty, but here it is literal: towering and vast like the great mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Himalayan describes the world's tallest mountains, so it means enormous, lofty and imposing.

clue.text: First-born voiced affectations

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: first-born children are heirs

explanation.surface: An eldest child speaks up about pretentious manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The H of heirs is silent, so it sounds identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs means adopting pretentious manners, so airs are showy affectations.

clue.text: Grill something with a sole

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to question someone closely for information
second meaning: a light shoe, which has a sole

explanation.walkthrough: With a fish called sole nearby, 'grill' looks like cooking; it means interrogate, and the sole is on a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to interrogate them for information, and a pump is a light slip-on shoe.

clue.text: Sweltering in rear of ship for PR event

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern
sweltering means very hot

explanation.surface: Baking at the back of a boat to promote some publicity stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear of ship' tempts you to take the last letter, P, but it is the whole word for the stern deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo opportunity is a staged moment arranged so the press can take pictures, a publicity occasion.

clue.text: Queen and King cast out losers, perfect!

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the Queen

indicators.note: metal cast in a new mould takes a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: R, Rex, abbreviates King
taken as written

explanation.surface: The royal couple banish the failures, and declare everything flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast out' reads as banish, but it signals the letters being reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no mistakes at all is flawless, which is the same as being faultless or ideal.

clue.text: In Vermont, a riotous part of N America

indicators.note: in says the word lies within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out in a US state, a rowdy corner of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Vermont itself is in North America, which makes it look like the definition; the comma and spaces are ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a province of Canada, so it is a region of the North American continent.

clue.text: Water running in vaults

definitions.meaning: first meaning: natural sources where water flows out of the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaults' suggests cellars where water might seep, but it is the verb for jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: Springs are places where groundwater flows up, and a person who leaps over something springs.

clue.text: Charm shown by a prince with ring

parts.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for prince
a peal is a ringing of bells
joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A royal suitor shows his charm by producing an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests jewellery, but it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is attractiveness or allure, the quality of drawing people in.

clue.text: Everyman's in lounge with drink, sweetie

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: to loll is to lounge lazily
the setter refers to himself, so his name gives the first person pronoun
pop is a fizzy drink
joins lounge and drink

explanation.surface: The setter relaxes in the lounge with a drink and a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' stands for 'is', and the setter's name means 'I', placed between the two other pieces. A sweetie is the British word for a sweet, or piece of candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard candy on a stick, which counts as a sweet or confection.

clue.text: Drifts — some of the Drifters?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: general gists or purports of a speech
second meaning: high male voices in the vocal group the Drifters

explanation.walkthrough: The Drifters were an American doo-wop and soul vocal group; some of its singers sang the high male part.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of an argument is its general meaning or gist, and tenor singers carry high male parts.

clue.text: Unacceptable, whichever way you look at it!

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: if the result is the same from either direction, it must read identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: a colloquial phrase for something not allowed, whose letters run the same in both directions

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a thing is out of order from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British informal speech for 'not acceptable', as in 'that's just not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying behaviour is not on means it is out of order and not to be tolerated.

clue.text: Brat in layette regularly in shock

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: horror is a feeling of shock

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A naughty child in its baby clothes is a shocking sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A layette is a set of clothes and bedding for a newborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy terror is an unruly, badly behaved child, which is exactly what a spoilt one is called.

clue.text: Loudly loads casks

indicators.note: loudly means said out for all to hear, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: loads as in lots, tons

explanation.surface: Someone noisily heaves barrels onto a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loads' looks like a verb for lifting cargo, but it means a great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large barrel for wine or beer, so tuns are big casks.

clue.text: Drivers should avoid these pets, only a pint drunk

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Motorists are told to steer clear of animals, and to have just a single pint.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, motoring offences earn marks on a driving licence; enough of them leads to a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalty points are endorsements added to a licence for traffic offences, which every motorist hopes never to get.
